slot.brief: Draw one card/ball from a well-defined set; compute P(A ∪ B) from given individual and joint probabilities using the addition rule.

stem: A card is drawn from a standard deck. Let $A$ be the event that it is red and $B$ the event that it is a king. Given $P(A)=\dfrac{1}{2}$, $P(B)=\dfrac{1}{13}$ and $P(A\cap B)=\dfrac{1}{26}$, find $P(A\cup B)$.
working:
$P(A\cup B)=P(A)+P(B)-P(A\cap B)$
$=\dfrac{1}{2}+\dfrac{1}{13}-\dfrac{1}{26}=\dfrac{7}{13}$.

Independent check: By inclusion–exclusion, P(A∪B)=1/2+1/13−1/26=7/13.
